Taste and smell work together, so when you have a cold and stuffy nose, food tastes weaker.
copy.tl:
Bakit mas mahina ang lasa kapag barado ang ilong?

Magkatuwang ang panlasa at pang-amoy, kaya kapag may sipon at barado ang ilong, mas mahina ang nararamdamang lasa.
copy.bis:
Nganong luya ang lami kung barado ang ilong?

Nagtinabangay ang panlasa ug panimaho, mao nga kung sip-on ug barado ang ilong, mas luya ang mabati nga lami.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Common signs of TB are a cough that lasts more than two weeks, fever, night sweats, and losing weight.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card lists symptoms of tuberculosis, a respiratory disease, but does not describe how any human body system (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) works. It shares the respiratory topic but provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Common signs of TB are a cough that lasts more than two weeks, fever, night sweats, and losing weight.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a cough, which relates to the respiratory system, but it does not identify the parts (nose, windpipe, lungs) or describe how they work. It is only tangentially related to the respiratory system.

copy.en: Common signs of TB are a cough that lasts more than two weeks, fever, night sweats, and losing weight.
copy.tl: Ang karaniwang sintomas ng TB ay matagal na ubo na lampas dalawang linggo, lagnat, pagpapawis sa gabi, at pagpapayat.
copy.bis: Ang kasagarang sintomas sa TB mao ang dugay nga ubo nga kapin sa duha ka semana, hilanat, pagpangsingot sa gabii, ug pagniwang.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the disease can become drug-resistant
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe natural selection as the primary mechanism driving evolutionary change
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about drug-resistant TB but does not describe natural selection as a mechanism or use secondary sources to explain evolutionary change. It only touches on a phenomenon that could be an example of evolution, without teaching the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the disease can become drug-resistant
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss in small groups important concepts in the theories of evolution, such as variation, heredity, isolation, selection, and adaptation
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions drug resistance but does not discuss variation, heredity, isolation, selection, or adaptation as concepts in evolutionary theory. It provides no instructional support for the listed concepts.

copy.en: If TB medicine isn't finished, the disease can become drug-resistant — a tougher kind that takes longer and is harder to cure.
copy.tl: Kapag hindi natapos ang gamot sa TB, maaari itong maging drug-resistant — isang uri na mas mahirap at mas matagal gamutin.
copy.bis: Kung dili mahuman ang tambal sa TB, mahimo kining drug-resistant — usa ka matang nga mas lisod ug mas dugay tambalan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it spreads when you breathe in air that has the bacteria in it
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions breathing air containing bacteria, which touches on the respiratory route, but it does not identify or describe the parts of the respiratory system (nose, windpipe, lungs) or how they work, nor does it use pictures/diagrams as required.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: air that has the bacteria in it
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that some organisms consist of a single cell (unicellular) like in bacteria and some consist of many cells (multicellular) like in a human
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions bacteria as the cause of TB, but it does not teach that bacteria are unicellular organisms or contrast unicellular with multicellular organisms. The focus is on transmission, not on cellular organization.

copy.en:
How does TB really spread?

TB is not spread by shaking hands or sharing plates — it spreads when you breathe in air that has the bacteria in it.
copy.tl:
Paano talaga kumakalat ang TB?

Hindi naikakalat ang TB sa simpleng paghawak ng kamay o paggamit ng iisang plato — kumakalat ito kapag humihinga ka ng hanging may bakterya.
copy.bis:
Giunsa gyud pagkatakod ang TB?

Ang TB dili matakod pinaagi sa paghikap sa kamot o paggamit og usa ka plato — motakod kini kon manginhawa ka og hangin nga adunay bakterya.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Show your teacher the problem and materials list before mixing!

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the problem and materials list, which are elements of a scientific investigation, but it does not describe the steps of a simple science investigation. copy.en: Show your teacher the problem and materials list before mixing! This fixes any unsafe or untestable plans right away.
copy.tl: Ipakita sa guro ang problema at listahan ng materyales bago maghalo! Para maayos agad kung may hindi ligtas o di kayang subukan.
copy.bis: Ipakita sa maestra ang problema ug lista sa materyales una mag-mix! Aron ma-ayo dayon kung naay dili luwas o dili pwede sulayan.

assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the number of teeth in an adult. It does not describe how any body system works, including the digestive system. Teeth are part of the digestive system, but the card provides no functional description, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An adult human has 32 teeth!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: using a labeled diagram, trace how food travels through the digestive tract and explain how different digestive processes work, including mechanical processing, secretion, digestion, absorption, and elimination
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires a labeled diagram tracing food through the digestive tract and explaining digestive processes. The card merely gives a tooth count, with no diagram, no tracing, and no explanation of digestive processes. It is only tangentially related to the digestive system.

copy.en:
How many teeth does an adult have?

An adult human has 32 teeth!
copy.tl:
Ilang ngipin ang mayroon ang isang adult?

May 32 na ngipin ang isang ganap na tao!
copy.bis:
Pila ka ngipon ang naa sa usa ka hamtong?

Ang usa ka hamtong nga tawo adunay 32 ka ngipon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Besides helping you eat, your teeth also help you speak words clearly.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and labeled diagrams the parts of the digestive system as mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, and large intestine, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions teeth helping with eating, which is a minor part of digestion, but it does not identify or describe the parts of the digestive system (mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, large intestine) or how they work. It is only tangentially related to the digestive system.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Besides helping you eat, your teeth also help you speak words clearly.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions teeth helping with eating and speech, but it does not describe how any of the listed body systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) work. It is a simple fact about teeth, not a description of a body system's function.

copy.en: Besides helping you eat, your teeth also help you speak words clearly.
copy.tl: Bukod sa pagkain, tumutulong din ang mga ngipin para makapagsalita tayo nang malinaw.
copy.bis: Gawas sa pagkaon, ang ngipon makatabang usab aron makasulti kita og tin-aw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The telephone was officially invented in the exact year 1876
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from the home or the local community to identify a science invention and explain its impact on their everyday life
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the year the telephone was invented. It does not use information from the home or local community, and it does not explain the invention's impact on everyday life, which are the core actions of G4-M-2.

copy.en:
Do you know what exact year the telephone was first invented in world history, kids?

The telephone was officially invented in the exact year 1876, which is super cool, kids!
copy.tl:
Alam mo ba kung anong taon naimbento ang telepono sa kasaysayan ng buong mundo, mga bata?

Ang telepono ay opisyal na naimbento noong taong 1876, napakagaling at nakakamangha 'di ba, mga bata!
copy.bis:
Nahibaw-an ba ka kung unsang tuig na-imbento ang telepono sa kasaysayan sa tibuok kalibutan, mga bata?

Ang telepono opisyal nga na-imbento niadtong tuig 1876, ka-galing ug grabe kahibulongan 'di ba, mga bata!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: termites have softer, paler bodies and are actually cousins of cockroaches, not ants
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a classification-like distinction (termites vs ants, cockroach relatives) but does not use a table and does not classify living things into the named groups (mammals, reptiles, insects, etc.). It only touches on insect relationships without the required format or scope.

copy.en:
Are termites just white ants?

No! Termites and ants both have queens, soldiers, and workers, but termites have softer, paler bodies and are actually cousins of cockroaches, not ants.
copy.tl:
Puting langgam ba ang anay?

Hindi! Kahit magkatulad sa reyna, sundalo, at manggagawa, mas malambot at maputi ang katawan ng anay, at ito pala ay kamag-anak ng ipis, hindi ng langgam.
copy.bis:
Puti ba nga hulmigas ang anay?

Dili! Bisan parehas og rayna, sundalo, ug trabahante, mas humok ug maputi ang lawas sa anay, ug kini diay paryente sa ipis, dili sa hulmigas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because termites eat the wooden parts of houses.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that termites eat wood, which is plant material, but it does not group termites into herbivore/carnivore/omnivore categories, nor does it use secondary sources to do so. It only provides a single fact about termite diet, not the classification skill required.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because termites eat the wooden parts of houses.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes termites eating wood, which is an interaction between a living thing and a non-living thing (wood from a house) that harms the house. However, it does not explain the interaction in terms of good or harm to the living things involved (termites benefit, but the card does not state this), nor does it address the broader concept of interactions bringing good or harm. It is a simple factual statement, not an explanation of the interaction's effects.

copy.en:
Why do termites damage houses?

Because termites eat the wooden parts of houses.
copy.tl:
Bakit nakakasira ng bahay ang anay?

Dahil kinakain ng anay ang kahoy na bahagi ng bahay.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga makaguba og balay ang anay?

Tungod kay gikaon sa anay ang kahoy nga bahin sa balay.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Wood is made of cellulose — and that's exactly what termites love to eat
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: A diet list is not grouping animals as herbivores, carnivores, or omnivores.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Wood is made of cellulose — and that's exactly what termites love to eat
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web
assignedReviews.reason: Eating wood in houses or furniture is not the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web.

copy.en:
Why do termites eat wood?

Wood is made of cellulose — and that's exactly what termites love to eat! It's not food for us, but for termites it's a nourishing meal, so they tunnel right through the wood.
copy.tl:
Bakit kinakain ng anay ang kahoy?

Gawa sa cellulose ang kahoy — at ito mismo ang paboritong kainin ng anay! Hindi ito pagkain para sa atin, pero masustansya ito para sa anay, kaya inuukit nila ang loob ng kahoy.
copy.bis:
Nganong gikaon sa anay ang kahoy?

Hinimo gikan sa cellulose ang kahoy — ug mao kini gyud ang paboritong kan-on sa anay! Dili kini pagkaon para kanato, apan nutrisyoso kini para sa anay, mao nga gibangagan nila ang sulod sa kahoy.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A termite queen can live for many years
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses lifespan, not the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). It is about a living thing but does not teach any of the listed characteristics.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A termite queen can live for many years
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions an animal's longevity but does not compare life-cycle stages or use a flow chart, which the competency explicitly requires. No direct support for the life-cycle comparison skill.

copy.en: A termite queen can live for many years — much longer than most other insects around her.
copy.tl: Ang reyna ng anay ay maaaring mabuhay ng maraming taon — mas matagal kaysa karaniwang insekto.
copy.bis: Ang reyna sa anay mahimong mabuhi og daghang tuig — mas dugay kaysa kasagarang insekto.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They reduce erosion because they slow down the water flowing down steep mountainsides!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains how terracing reduces erosion by slowing water flow, but it does not demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials. It addresses erosion prevention rather than the transport process itself, so it only shares the broad topic of erosion.

copy.en:
How do step-like terraces like the Banaue Rice Terraces reduce erosion?

They reduce erosion because they slow down the water flowing down steep mountainsides!
copy.tl:
Paano pumipigil sa erosion ang hagdan-hagdang taniman tulad ng Banaue Rice Terraces?

Pumipigil ito sa erosion dahil pinapabagal nito ang agos ng tubig pababa sa matarik na gilid ng bundok!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagpugong sa erosion sa hagdan-hagdan nga taniman sama sa Banaue Rice Terraces?

Mopugong kini sa erosion tungod kay gipahinay niini ang dagayday sa tubig paubos sa tarik nga kilid sa bukid!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it can take several days after a wound before muscles start to stiffen
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions muscle stiffening due to tetanus, but it does not describe how the muscular system (or any body system) works. It is about a disease symptom, not the function of a body system, so it only shares the topic of muscles.

copy.en: Tetanus doesn't show up right away—it can take several days after a wound before muscles start to stiffen, even if the wound looks healed.
copy.tl: Hindi agad lumalabas ang tetanus—ilang araw munang lumilipas bago tumigas ang kalamnan, kahit gumaling na ang itsura ng sugat.
copy.bis: Dili dayon mogawas ang tetanus—molabay usa og pipila ka adlaw una motikig ang kaunuran, bisan og naayo na ang dagway sa samad.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The intertidal zone is the shore area between the high tide mark and the low tide mark
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a habitat (the intertidal zone) and its tidal exposure, but does not address the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter). It shares the broad topic of living things and environment but provides no direct instructional support for identifying basic needs.

copy.en: The intertidal zone is the area where the sea meets the land between high and low tides, and it is also called the foreshore or seashore.
copy.tl: Ang intertidal zone ay ang lugar kung saan nagtatagpo ang dagat at lupa sa pagitan ng high tide at low tide, at tinatawag din itong foreshore o seashore.
copy.bis: Ang intertidal zone mao ang lugar diin ang dagat ug yuta magtagbo tali sa high tide ug low tide, ug gitawag usab kini nga foreshore o seashore.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The Sun as an energy source is unrelated to identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: Solar energy is unrelated to the five body systems.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that the Sun provides energy, which is a general prerequisite for photosynthesis, but it does not describe the process of photosynthesis or respiration, nor identify raw materials and products. It shares the broad topic of energy but provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: The sun is the main source of heat and light, and almost all living things rely on its steady warmth and brightness.
copy.tl: Ang araw ang pangunahing pinagmumulan ng init at liwanag, at halos lahat ng may buhay ay umaasa sa init at liwanag nito.
copy.bis: Ang adlaw mao ang nag-unang tinubdan sa init ug kahayag, ug halos tanang buhing butang nagsalig sa kainit ug kahayag niini.

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes macroscopic thermal expansion of bridges and rails but does not mention particles, their motion, spacing, attraction, or increased speed with temperature. It does not directly support the particle-model competency.

copy.en: During the Philippine hot season in April and May, bridges and rail tracks expand a lot! Keeping expansion joints safe is super important for everyone.
copy.tl: Sa mainit na tag-araw sa Pilipinas noong Abril at Mayo, malaki ang pagpapalawak ng mga tulay at riles! Mahalagang ingatan ang expansion joints para sa kaligtasan ng lahat.
copy.bis: Sa init nga tag-init sa Pilipinas sa Abril ug Mayo, dako ang pagpapalawak sa mga tulay ug riles! Importante nga atimanon ang expansion joints para sa kaligtasan sa tanan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because the air expands!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe that particles are constantly in motion, have spaces between them, attract each other, and move faster as the temperature increases (or with the addition of heat)
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains a macroscopic effect (air expands when hot) but does not describe particles, their motion, spacing, attraction, or that they move faster with temperature. It does not directly teach the particle model competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Why does air pressure inside a car tyre rise in hot weather?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes in properties of materials when exposed to certain changes in temperature, such as changes when wood or coal are burned
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a change in a material (air) with temperature, but the competency focuses on changes in properties of materials like wood or coal when burned. The card does not address burning or the specific property changes described in the competency.

copy.en:
Why does air pressure inside a car tyre rise in hot weather?

Because the air expands! That is why you should check the tyre pressure carefully, especially before long trips.
copy.tl:
Bakit tumataas ang air pressure sa loob ng gulong ng sasakyan sa mainit na panahon?

Dahil nagpapalawak ang hangin! Kaya dapat pagmasdan nang maayos ang tyre pressure, lalo na bago ang mahabang biyahe.
copy.bis:
Nganong motaas ang air pressure sulod sa gulong sa sasakyan sa init nga panahon?

Tungod kay nagpapalawak ang hangin! Mao nga angay i-tsek og maayo ang tyre pressure, ilabina sa wala pa ang taas nga biyahe.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe that particles are constantly in motion, have spaces between them, attract each other, and move faster as the temperature increases (or with the addition of heat)

assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about identifying and using measurement units (mg, g, kg, °C). The card contains no units, measurements, or unit usage, so it is unrelated.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Inside a liquid thermometer, the liquid rises up when it gets hot because it expands!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe different science process skills used in performing simple science activities, such as observing, predicting, and measuring using units such as millimeter, centimeter, and meter
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about describing science process skills such as observing, predicting, and measuring with length units. The card does not address any process skill or unit; it only explains thermometer expansion.

copy.en: Inside a liquid thermometer, the liquid rises up when it gets hot because it expands!
copy.tl: Sa loob ng isang liquid thermometer, tumataas ang likido kapag uminit dahil lumalawak ito!
copy.bis: Sa sulod sa usa ka liquid thermometer, mosaka ang likido kon mainit kay molapad kini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The gap between the walls blocks the heat from escaping.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions heat escaping but does not identify any specific mode (conduction, convection, radiation) or give advantageous/disadvantageous examples. It only states a general insulation effect.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The gap between the walls blocks the heat from escaping.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain in terms of the particle model the processes underlying convection and conduction of heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not explain heat transfer using the particle model, nor does it address conduction or convection specifically. It only describes a double-wall gap blocking heat, which is not direct support for the competency.

copy.en:
How does a thermos keep your drink hot for so long?

A drink stays hot inside a thermos because of its double wall! The gap between the walls blocks the heat from escaping.
copy.tl:
Paano nananatiling mainit ang inumin mo sa loob ng thermos?

Nanatiling mainit ang inumin sa thermos dahil sa double wall nito! Ang gap sa pagitan ng mga dingding ay humahadlang sa init na tumakas.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagpabiling init sa imong ilimnon sulod sa thermos?

Magpabiling init ang ilimnon sulod sa thermos tungod sa double wall niini! Ang gap sa taliwala sa mga bongbong nagababag sa init nga moikyas.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes viscosity (thickness) of a liquid affecting sinking speed, but G5-M-3 requires describing properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume. Viscosity is not shape or volume, so the card does not directly support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A marble sinks more slowly through honey than water because honey is thicker!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses how the liquid's thickness affects the movement of an object, but G3-F-2 focuses on object properties (size, shape, heaviness, material, surface texture) that affect movement. The card does not address any of these object characteristics, so it is only related to the topic of movement.

copy.en: A marble sinks more slowly through honey than water because honey is thicker!
copy.tl: Mas mabagal lumubog ang holen sa pulot kaysa tubig dahil mas malapot ang pulot!
copy.bis: Mas hinay molugdang ang holen sa dugos kay sa tubig tungod kay mas baga ang dugos!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most modern wind turbines have three long blades that spin in the wind.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe kinetic energy as the movement of objects or particles, and potential energy as energy stored due to the position of objects or particles
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions spinning blades, which involve movement, but it does not describe kinetic energy as movement of objects/particles or potential energy as stored energy. It provides no instructional support for the competency's core concepts.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most modern wind turbines have three long blades that spin in the wind.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe examples of accelerating objects at school and in the local community, including objects that show uniform circular motion
assignedReviews.reason: The card notes that blades spin, which could be an example of circular motion, but it does not describe acceleration or uniform circular motion, nor does it ask students to observe or describe such examples. The content is too superficial to directly support the competency.

copy.en: Most modern wind turbines have three long blades that spin in the wind.
copy.tl: Karamihan sa makabagong turbina ng hangin ay may tatlong mahahabang aspas.
copy.bis: Kasagaran sa modernong turbine sa hangin adunay tulo ka tag-as nga pako.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They are igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: classify common rocks from provided samples using a simple rock classification system, such as a dichotomous key

assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why a touchscreen responds to a bare finger due to the body's electrical conductivity, touching on the concept of conductors/insulators. However, the competency requires designing and constructing a simple electrical circuit to test materials for conductivity. The card provides no instruction or support for circuit design, construction, or testing, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Why does a touchscreen need your bare finger?

Our bodies carry a little electricity! The screen senses this where your finger touches, which is why it won't work if you wear thick gloves.
copy.tl:
Bakit kailangan ng touchscreen ang hubad mong daliri?

May konting kuryente ang katawan natin! Nararamdaman ito ng screen sa hawak ng daliri mo, kaya hindi ito gagana kung may suot kang makapal na guwantes.
copy.bis:
Nganong kinahanglan sa touchscreen ang imong hubad nga tudlo?

Ang atong lawas adunay gamay nga kuryente! Mabati kini sa screen kung asa midapat ang imong tudlo, mao nga dili mogana kung magsul-ob ka ug baga nga gwantes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You inherit traits like your height or hair color from your parents' genes!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that genetic information is passed on to offspring from both parents by the process of meiosis and fertilization
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that traits are inherited from parents' genes, but does not mention meiosis, fertilization, or the mechanism by which genetic information is passed from both parents. It only touches the general idea of inheritance, not the specific process required by the competency.

copy.en: You inherit traits like your height or hair color from your parents' genes!
copy.tl: Minamana mo ang mga katangian tulad ng taas o kulay ng buhok mula sa mga gene ng iyong mga magulang!
copy.bis: Mapanunod nimo ang mga kinaiya sama sa katas-on o kolor sa buhok gikan sa mga gene sa imong mga ginikanan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The transistor was invented in the year 1947 at Bell Labs!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from the home or the local community to identify a science invention and explain its impact on their everyday life
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies a science invention (transistor) but does not use information from the home or local community, nor does it explain the impact on everyday life as required by the competency. It only states the year and a general importance for technology.

copy.en: The transistor was invented in the year 1947 at Bell Labs! It was a very important invention for technology.
copy.tl: Ang transistor ay naimbento noong 1947 sa Bell Labs! Ito ay isang napakahalagang imbensyon para sa teknolohiya.
copy.bis: Ang transistor gi-imbento niadtong 1947 sa Bell Labs! Kini usa kaimportante kaayo nga imbensyon alang sa teknolohiya.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The chromium forms a thin protective layer that stops rust.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions rust resistance, which is a chemical behavior, but it does not describe chemical properties such as being burnt, reacting with other materials, or being degradable/biodegradable as required by the competency. It only gives a specific example of corrosion prevention without teaching the general concept.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They are made of stainless steel, a mix of iron and chromium!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card calls stainless steel a mix of iron and chromium, but it does not describe uniform or non-uniform mixtures, solutions, or suspensions, nor does it explain the concept of mixtures. The mention of a mix is incidental and does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Why don't our kitchen pots and knives rust easily?

They are made of stainless steel, a mix of iron and chromium! The chromium forms a thin protective layer that stops rust.
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi madaling kalawangin ang mga kaldero at kutsilyo natin?

Gawa sila sa stainless steel, halo ng iron at chromium! Gumagawa ang chromium ng manipis na layer na pumipigil sa kalawang.
copy.bis:
Nganong dili dali motaya ang atong mga kaldero ug kutsilyo?

Hinimo kini sa stainless steel, sagol sa iron ug chromium! Ang chromium maghimo og nipis nga layer nga mopugong sa taya.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Clean glass, clear water, and a sparkling clean window are all perfect examples of transparent things!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives examples of transparent things (glass, water, window) but does not describe physical properties of solid materials as required by G3-M-5. Transparency is a physical property, but the competency focuses on solids and examples like hard, shiny, or stretchable. The card includes a liquid (water) and does not explain or describe the property, so it only shares vocabulary with the competency.

copy.en: Clean glass, clear water, and a sparkling clean window are all perfect examples of transparent things!
copy.tl: Ang malinis na bildo, malinaw na tubig, at kinintab na bintana ay mga magagandang halimbawa ng transparent na bagay!
copy.bis: Ang limpyo nga bildo, tin-aw nga tubig, ug kinintab nga bintana maoy mga nindong panig-ingnan sa transparent nga butang!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Studying tree rings to find out a tree's age and the dates it lived through is called dendrochronology.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how plant organs (leaf, stem, roots) work together as the transport system
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses tree rings (a stem feature) but does not describe how leaf, stem, and roots work together as a transport system. No transport content is present.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Studying tree rings to find out a tree's age and the dates it lived through is called dendrochronology.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions determining a tree's age, which relates to growth, but does not describe the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). It does not teach the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Studying tree rings to find out a tree's age and the dates it lived through is called dendrochronology.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the purpose of specialized structures in plants, such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, and aerial roots
assignedReviews.reason: Tree rings are a plant structure, but the card does not describe the purpose of specialized structures such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, or aerial roots. No direct support for the competency.

copy.en:
What's the science of tree rings called?

Studying tree rings to find out a tree's age and the dates it lived through is called dendrochronology.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pag-aaral ng singsing ng puno?

Ang pag-aaral ng mga singsing ng puno para malaman ang edad at petsa nito ay tinatawag na dendrochronology.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pagtuon sa singsing sa kahoy?

Ang pagtuon sa mga singsing sa kahoy aron mahibaw-an ang gulang ug petsa niini gitawag og dendrochronology.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a big share of the world's oxygen also comes from tiny ocean plants called plankton
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that plankton produce oxygen, which is a product of photosynthesis, but it does not describe the process of photosynthesis or respiration, nor identify raw materials and products. It provides background context about oxygen sources but does not directly support the competency's instructional goal.

copy.en:
Are trees the only source of oxygen?

Many think only trees make oxygen. Trees do help a lot, but a big share of the world's oxygen also comes from tiny ocean plants called plankton.
copy.tl:
Puno lang ba ang gumagawa ng oxygen?

Akala ng marami, puno lang ang gumagawa ng oxygen. Totoo na malaki ang tulong ng puno, pero malaking bahagi ng oxygen sa mundo ay galing din sa maliliit na halaman sa dagat na tinatawag na plankton.
copy.bis:
Kahoy ra ba ang naghimo og oxygen?

Daghan ang naghunahuna nga kahoy ra ang naghimo og oxygen. Tinuod nga dako ang tabang sa kahoy, apan dakong bahin sa oxygen sa kalibotan naggikan usab sa gagmay nga tanom sa dagat nga gitawag og plankton.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Trees are the biggest and longest-living plants
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses trees as large and long-lived plants, but it does not address outer plant parts such as leaves, roots, or stems, nor their role in obtaining water and nutrients from the soil.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Trees are the biggest and longest-living plants
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions longevity and size, but does not describe the characteristics of living things specified in the competency: growing, responding, and reproducing.

copy.en:
Which plants live the longest?

Trees are the biggest and longest-living plants — some live for hundreds of years because their hard wood gives them strength!
copy.tl:
Aling halaman ang pinakamatagal mabuhay?

Ang mga puno ang pinakamalaki at pinakamatagal mabuhay na halaman — may nabubuhay ng daan-daang taon dahil sa lakas ng matigas nilang kahoy!
copy.bis:
Unsang tanom ang labing dugay mabuhi?

Ang mga kahoy mao ang labing dako ug labing dugay mabuhi nga tanom — ang uban mabuhi og gatusan ka tuig tungod sa kusog sa ilang gahi nga kahoy!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: About 20 centimeters long -- as long as a banana!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the size of a T. rex tooth. It does not describe an outer body part such as head, legs, or wings, nor does it identify any role of the tooth in movement or gathering food. The content is only tangentially about an animal body part.

copy.en:
How big was a T. rex tooth?

About 20 centimeters long -- as long as a banana!
copy.tl:
Gaano kahaba ang ngipin ng T. rex?

Umaabot ito ng mga 20 sentimetro ang haba -- kasinghaba ng saging!
copy.bis:
Unsa kataas ang ngipon sa T. rex?

Moabot kini og mga 20 ka sentimetro ang gitas-on -- sama kataas sa saging!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Triceratops means 'three-horned face' — a perfect name for this dinosaur with three horns on its head!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card only explains the meaning of the name and notes the presence of three horns. It does not describe the outer body parts' role in movement or gathering food, which is the focus of G3-L-4.

copy.en:
What does 'Triceratops' mean?

Triceratops means 'three-horned face' — a perfect name for this dinosaur with three horns on its head!
copy.tl:
Ano ang ibig sabihin ng 'Triceratops'?

Ang Triceratops ay nangangahulugang 'mukhang may tatlong sungay' — bagay na bagay dahil may tatlong sungay ito sa ulo!
copy.bis:
Unsay pasabot sa 'Triceratops'?

Ang Triceratops nagpasabot og 'nawong nga adunay tulo ka sungay' — angay kaayo kay adunay tulo ka sungay kini sa ulo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Triton is the only large moon that orbits its planet backwards (retrograde)!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card presents a single fact about Triton's retrograde orbit. It does not describe the general structure of the solar system, nor does it identify major celestial objects, their main features, or general composition as required by the competency. The content is only tangentially related to the solar system.

copy.en:
What makes Triton's orbit so special?

Triton is the only large moon that orbits its planet backwards (retrograde)!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nagpapatangi sa pag-ikot ng Triton?

Ito ang tanging malaking buwan na umiikot nang pabaligtad (retrograde) sa planeta nito!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang nakahimo nga espesyal ang paglibot sa Triton?

Kini mao lang ang dakong bulan nga mulibot nga pabalik (retrograde) sa iyang planeta!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When spinning fast, it stands like a tiny top!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and demonstrate different ways to make objects move by natural causes, such as wind and water, or by people, such as pushing, pulling, rolling, and carrying
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the behavior of a spinning coin (standing, wobbling, falling) but does not explore or demonstrate ways to make objects move via natural causes or by pushing, pulling, rolling, or carrying. It is only tangentially about motion.

copy.en:
Ever wonder why a spinning coin stands on its edge?

When spinning fast, it stands like a tiny top! As it slows, it wobbles and falls flat. The exact same spinning principle is at work here.
copy.tl:
Napapaisip ka ba kung bakit tumatayo ang barya sa gilid kapag pinaikot?

Kapag mabilis umiikot, tumatayo ito na parang maliit na trompo! Kapag bumagal, nag-uuga ito at natutumbang patag. Parehong prinsipyo ng pag-ikot ang gumagana rito.
copy.bis:
Nahunahuna ba nimo ngano motindog ang sensilyo sa ngilit kung patuyokon?

Kung paspas magtuyok, motindog kini sama sa gamay nga trompo! Kung mohinay, mouyog kini ug matumba nga patag. Parehong prinsipyo sa pagtuyok ang naglihok dinhi.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: How high does the troposphere reach from the ground?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the height range of the troposphere. It does not explain how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere, which is the focus of G7-E-9.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: How high does the troposphere reach from the ground?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a physical model or use drawings to demonstrate how the tilt of the Earth relative to its orbit around the Sun affects the intensity of sunlight absorbed by different areas of Earth over a year
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about the troposphere's height, not about the tilt of the Earth relative to its orbit and its effect on sunlight intensity. It does not support the competency's content or required model/drawing activity.

copy.en:
How high does the troposphere reach from the ground?

It reaches about 8 kilometers at the poles and up to 18 kilometers near the equator!
copy.tl:
Hanggang saan abot ng troposphere mula sa lupa?

Umaabot ito ng mga 8 kilometro sa mga poste at 18 kilometro malapit sa ekwador!
copy.bis:
Hangtod asa moabot ang troposphere gikan sa yuta?

Mokab-ot kini og mga 8 ka kilometro sa mga poste ug 18 ka kilometro duol sa ekwador!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a tsunami can happen without an earthquake
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how earthquakes result in tsunamis that devastate shoreline communities
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires explaining how earthquakes result in tsunamis. The card explicitly states a tsunami can happen without an earthquake and describes a volcano-collapse tsunami, which contradicts the earthquake-tsunami mechanism rather than supporting it.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a sea volcano's side collapsed and caused a tsunami
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain what volcanoes are and how they are formed
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a volcano but does not explain what volcanoes are or how they are formed. It only uses a volcano as the cause of a tsunami, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Did you know a tsunami can happen without an earthquake?

Yes! In 2018 in Indonesia, our neighbor, a sea volcano's side collapsed and caused a tsunami — no strong earthquake needed!
copy.tl:
Alam mo bang pwedeng magkaroon ng tsunami kahit walang lindol?

Oo! Noong 2018 sa Indonesia, kapitbahay natin, gumuho ang gilid ng bulkan sa dagat at gumawa ng tsunami — walang malakas na lindol!
copy.bis:
Nahibalo ka ba nga mahimong mag tsunami bisan walay linog?

Oo! Niadtong 2018 sa Indonesia, silingan natong nasud, natumpag ang kilid sa bulkan sa dagat ug naghimo og tsunami — walay kusog nga linog!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sometimes there is a loud roar like a train or airplane before a tsunami arrives, so you should run right away.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe procedures that the authorities have in place to alert communities of pending tsunamis and what procedures can be implemented should a tsunami impact a community
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a natural warning sign (loud roar) and a personal action (run), but does not describe procedures that authorities have in place to alert communities or procedures implemented when a tsunami impacts a community. It shares the tsunami safety topic but does not directly support the competency's focus on official alert and response procedures.

copy.en: Sometimes there is a loud roar like a train or airplane before a tsunami arrives, so you should run right away.
copy.tl: Minsan ay may malakas na ugong na parang tren o eroplano bago dumating ang tsunami, kaya dapat agad tumakbo.
copy.bis: Usahay adunay kusog nga dahunog nga sama sa tren o eroplano sa dili pa moabot ang tsunami, mao nga kinahanglan dayon modagan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It comes from an earthquake and carries enormous energy.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how earthquakes result in tsunamis that devastate shoreline communities
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that a tsunami originates from an earthquake and carries energy, but it does not explain how earthquakes result in tsunamis or how they devastate shoreline communities. This is background knowledge, not direct instruction for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Is a tsunami just like the daily rising and falling of the tide?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: relate the relative movements of the Earth, Moon, and Sun with the occurrence of tides
assignedReviews.reason: The card contrasts a tsunami with an ordinary tide, but it does not relate the relative movements of the Earth, Moon, and Sun with the occurrence of tides. The mention of tide is only to distinguish tsunami from it; no tidal mechanism is taught.

copy.en:
Is a tsunami just like the daily rising and falling of the tide?

Even though a tsunami is low at sea, it is not like the ordinary daily tide! It comes from an earthquake and carries enormous energy.
copy.tl:
Parang ordinaryong pagtaas-baba ba ng tubig sa dalampasigan ang tsunami?

Kahit mababa rin sa dagat ang tsunami, hindi ito gaya ng karaniwang pagtaas-baba ng tubig! Galing ito sa lindol at dala nito ang napakalaking lakas.
copy.bis:
Sama ba sa naandang pagsaka-kanaog sa taob ang tsunami?

Bisan ubos usab sa dagat ang tsunami, dili kini sama sa naandang adlaw-adlaw nga pagsaka-kanaog! Naggikan kini sa linog ug nagdala og dako kaayo nga kusog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A tsunami is a series of waves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how earthquakes result in tsunamis that devastate shoreline communities
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that a tsunami is a series of waves and that later waves can be larger. It does not explain how earthquakes result in tsunamis or how tsunamis devastate shoreline communities, which are the core actions of G7-E-7.

copy.en:
Is a tsunami just one single wave?

Nope! A tsunami is a series of waves, and the second or third wave can actually be even bigger!
copy.tl:
Isang alon lang ba ang tsunami?

Hindi! Ang tsunami ay serye ng mga alon, at ang pangalawa o pangatlo ay maaaring mas malaki pa!
copy.bis:
Usa ra ba ka balod ang tsunami?

Dili! Ang tsunami serye sa mga balod, ug ang ikaduha o ikatulo mahimong mas dako pa!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A volcanic eruption or a big underwater landslide can also cause a tsunami!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how earthquakes result in tsunamis that devastate shoreline communities
assignedReviews.reason: The card lists non-earthquake causes of tsunamis (volcanic eruption, underwater landslide). It does not explain how earthquakes result in tsunamis or their devastation of shoreline communities, so it only shares the tsunami topic without supporting the earthquake-specific competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A volcanic eruption or a big underwater landslide can also cause a tsunami!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain what volcanoes are and how they are formed
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions volcanic eruption as a tsunami trigger but does not explain what volcanoes are or how they are formed. It only uses the word 'volcanic' in a different context, providing no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en:
What else can start a tsunami besides earthquakes?

A volcanic eruption or a big underwater landslide can also cause a tsunami!
copy.tl:
Ano pa ang pwedeng mag-umpisa ng tsunami bukod sa lindol?

Ang pagsabog ng bulkan o malaking pagguho ng lupa sa ilalim ng dagat ay pwede ring mag-umpisa ng tsunami!
copy.bis:
Unsa pa ang makapapukan og tsunami gawas sa linog?

Ang pagbuto sa bulkan o dakong pagguho sa yuta ilawom sa dagat makapapukan usab og tsunami!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The tokay gecko (tuko) is much bigger than the common house lizard (butiki)
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card only compares the sizes of two lizards. It does not use a table, does not classify living things into the named groups (e.g., reptiles, mammals, insects), and provides no information about similar characteristics used for classification.

copy.en:
Which is bigger, the tuko or the butiki?

The tokay gecko (tuko) is much bigger than the common house lizard (butiki) — a small butiki fits in your palm, but a tuko can be as long as a hand-span or more!
copy.tl:
Alin mas malaki, ang tuko o ang butiki?

Mas malaki ang tuko kaysa karaniwang butiki sa bahay — ang maliit na butiki ay kasya sa palad, pero ang tuko ay umaabot ng halos isang dangkal o higit pa!
copy.bis:
Hain mas dako, ang tuko o ang tabili?

Mas dako ang tuko kaysa sa kasagarang tabili sa balay — ang gamayng tabili mahaom ra sa palad, apan ang tuko makaabot og hapit usa ka dangaw o sobra pa!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The best, freshest yellowfin tuna caught in the Philippines is exported to other countries
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a Philippine animal (yellowfin tuna) but does not classify it by habitat, nor does it use a drawing or diagram. The content is about export and sashimi, not about terrestrial/aquatic/aerial classification.

copy.en: The best, freshest yellowfin tuna caught in the Philippines is exported to other countries, where it's often made into sashimi.
copy.tl: Ang pinakasariwa at pinakamasarap na yellowfin tuna mula sa Pilipinas ay ipinapadala sa ibang bansa, kung saan kadalasan itong ginagawang sashimi.
copy.bis: Ang labing presko ug labing lami nga yellowfin tuna gikan sa Pilipinas ipadala sa ubang nasod, diin sagad kining himoong sashimi.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Turmeric is a root that gives a bright yellow color
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes turmeric as a root used for dyeing food and cloth, mentioning its bright yellow color. It does not describe physical properties of solid materials such as hardness, shininess, or stretchability as required by the competency. The color mention is only a superficial link to material properties.

copy.en: Turmeric is a root that gives a bright yellow color, used to color our food and sometimes even cloth!
copy.tl: Ang turmeric ay isang ugat na nagbibigay ng matingkad na dilaw na kulay, ginagamit para kulayan ang ating pagkain at minsan ang tela!
copy.bis: Ang turmeric usa ka gamot nga naghatag og hayag nga dalag nga kolor, gigamit aron koloran ang atong pagkaon ug usahay ang panapton!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The shell is attached to its spine and ribs, so it's part of the turtle's body
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the turtle's shell as an outer body part but does not identify its role in movement or gathering food, which is the core action of G3-L-4. It only states that the shell is attached to the spine and ribs, providing no functional role related to moving or feeding.

copy.en:
Can a turtle leave its shell?

No! The shell is attached to its spine and ribs, so it's part of the turtle's body — just like you can't take off your own skin.
copy.tl:
Kaya bang lumabas ng pagong sa talukab?

Hindi! Ang talukab ay nakakabit sa gulugod at tadyang nito, kaya parte ito ng katawan — parang hindi mo rin kayang tanggalin ang iyong balat.
copy.bis:
Makagawas ba ang bao sa iyang talukab?

Dili! Ang talukab nakadikit sa iyang gulugod ug gusok, busa bahin kini sa lawas — sama nga dili nimo matangtang ang imong panit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The turtle's heart, lungs, and stomach all live inside the shell
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the turtle's shell as an outer body part, but focuses on its protective function and the internal organs inside, not on the role of outer body parts (head, legs, wings) in movement or gathering food as required by the competency.

copy.en:
Is a turtle's shell hollow inside?

No! The turtle's heart, lungs, and stomach all live inside the shell — so it's like a protective room for its body, not an empty space.
copy.tl:
Guwang ba ang loob ng talukab ng pagong?

Hindi! Naninirahan sa loob ng talukab ang puso, baga, at sikmura ng pagong — parang isang protektadong silid ito ng katawan nito, hindi ito walang laman.
copy.bis:
Guwang ba ang sulod sa talukab sa bao?

Dili! Ang kasingkasing, baga, ug tiyan sa bao anaa sa sulod sa talukab — sama kini sa panalipod nga lawak sa iyang lawas, dili kini walay sulod.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sometimes a dragonfly eats the insect it caught while it's still flying through the air.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that a dragonfly eats insects, which is a fact about its diet, but it does not group animals into herbivores, carnivores, or omnivores, nor does it use secondary sources to do so. It provides a single dietary example without the classification action required by the competency.

copy.en: Sometimes a dragonfly eats the insect it caught while it's still flying through the air.
copy.tl: Minsan ay kinakain ng tutubi ang nahuli nitong insekto habang lumilipad pa ito sa hangin.
copy.bis: Usahay ang alindahaw mokaon sa nadakpan niini nga insekto samtang naglupad pa kini sa hangin.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Tuyo is fish that's been salted and dried in the sun!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions as applied in food preservation and materials production, control of fire, pollution, and corrosion
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions food preservation (salted and dried fish) but does not explain any factor affecting the rate of chemical reactions, such as temperature, water activity, or concentration. It only states that salting and drying help the fish last, without connecting this to reaction rates or chemical processes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Tuyo is fish that's been salted and dried in the sun!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate various techniques in separating mixtures, such as decantation, winnowing, scooping, picking, evaporation, filtering, sieving, and using magnets
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes salting and sun-drying as preservation methods, but it does not demonstrate or explain any mixture separation technique such as evaporation, filtering, sieving, or decantation. Drying fish is not presented as a separation technique, and no procedure or demonstration is included.

copy.en:
Ever wonder how tuyo lasts so long?

Tuyo is fish that's been salted and dried in the sun! That's why it can last for many days without spoiling.
copy.tl:
Alam mo ba kung paano tumatagal ang tuyo nang matagal?

Ang tuyo ay isdang inasnan at ibinilad sa araw! Kaya tumatagal ito nang maraming araw na hindi nasisira.
copy.bis:
Nahibaw-an ba nimo kung giunsa pagdugay sa bulad (tuyo)?

Ang bulad (tuyo) kay isda nga giasinan ug gibulad sa adlaw! Mao nga modugay kini og daghang adlaw nga dili madunot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Dogs, cats, and horses can swivel their ears toward a sound.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes ears as outer body parts and their role in hearing and movement, but the competency specifically requires identifying the role of outer body parts to move and to gather food. Ears are not involved in gathering food, and the card does not address food gathering at all. It only touches on movement (swiveling ears, turning head), so it does not directly support the stated skill.

copy.en:
Why can dogs move their ears but not you?

Dogs, cats, and horses can swivel their ears toward a sound. We humans can't move our ears, so we turn our whole head instead!
copy.tl:
Bakit kaya nilang igalaw ang tainga?

Kayang igalaw ng aso, pusa, at kabayo ang kanilang tainga papunta sa tunog. Tayo, hindi — kaya inililingon na lang natin ang buong ulo!
copy.bis:
Nganong makalihok ang ilang dalunggan?

Makalihok ang dalunggan sa iro, iring, ug kabayo padulong sa tingog. Kita, dili — mao nga molingi na lang ta sa tibuok ulo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Two ears are needed for good direction-finding.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains how two ears help locate the direction of a sound, but does not describe how sound is made or transferred, which is the focus of G3-F-4. It shares the topic of sound but provides no direct instructional support for the competency's stated skill.

copy.en:
Why are two ears better than one?

With only one ear working, it's harder to tell where sound comes from, the brain has nothing to compare. Two ears are needed for good direction-finding.
copy.tl:
Bakit mas mabuti ang dalawang tainga?

Kapag isang tainga lang ang gumagana, mas mahirap malaman kung saan galing ang tunog dahil walang maikukumpara ang utak. Kailangan ang dalawang tainga para sa magandang pagtukoy ng direksyon.
copy.bis:
Nganong mas maayo ang duha ka dalunggan?

Kung usa ra ka dalunggan ang molihok, mas lisod mahibal-an kung asa gikan ang tingog kay walay ikatandi ang utok. Kinahanglan ang duha ka dalunggan para maayo ang pagtino sa direksyon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Together, your two feet have 52 bones — 26 in each foot!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states a trivia fact about the number of bones in the feet. It does not describe how the skeletal system works, nor does it explain any function or process of the skeletal system as required by G4-L-1.

copy.en:
How many bones do your two feet have?

Together, your two feet have 52 bones — 26 in each foot!
copy.tl:
Ilang buto ang mayroon ang dalawang paa mo?

Kapag pinagsama, may 52 buto ang dalawang paa mo — 26 bawat paa!
copy.bis:
Pila ka bukog ang duha nimo ka tiil?

Kung tingbon, ang duha ka tiil adunay 52 ka bukog — 26 sa matag tiil!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Type A blood has the A antigen, while type B blood has the B antigen on its red cells
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: ABO antigens are typing, not identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels and how they work.

copy.en: Type A blood has the A antigen, while type B blood has the B antigen on its red cells.
copy.tl: Ang dugong uri A ay may A antigen, habang ang uri B ay may B antigen sa mga pulang selula nito.
copy.bis: Ang dugo nga klase A adunay A antigen, samtang ang klase B adunay B antigen sa mga pula niini nga selula.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: their child can be type AB — taking the A gene from one parent and the B gene from the other
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: represent patterns of inheritance of a simple dominant/ recessive characteristic through generations of a family
assignedReviews.reason: The card illustrates inheritance of ABO blood type, which involves multiple alleles and codominance, not a simple dominant/recessive characteristic. It does not represent a family pedigree or generations, so it does not directly support G8-L-4.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: their child can be type AB — taking the A gene from one parent and the B gene from the other
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: predict simple ratios of offspring genotypes and phenotypes in crosses involving dominant/recessive gene pairs
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a single example of an AB child from pure A and pure B parents, but it does not predict ratios of genotypes or phenotypes in dominant/recessive crosses. ABO inheritance is not a simple dominant/recessive gene pair, so it does not directly support G8-L-5.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: taking the A gene from one parent and the B gene from the other
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that genetic information is passed on to offspring from both parents by the process of meiosis and fertilization
assignedReviews.reason: The card shows that offspring receive genetic information from both parents, which is background for understanding meiosis and fertilization. However, it does not explain the processes of meiosis or fertilization, so it is not direct support for G7-L-6.

copy.en: If one parent is pure type A and the other pure type B, their child can be type AB — taking the A gene from one parent and the B gene from the other!
copy.tl: Kung ang isang magulang ay puro type A at ang isa ay puro type B, maaaring maging type AB ang anak nila dahil kukuha ito ng A gene sa isa at B gene sa isa pa!
copy.bis: Kung ang usa ka ginikanan puro type A ug ang lain puro type B, mahimong type AB ang ilang anak tungod kay mokuha kini og A gene gikan sa usa ug B gene gikan sa lain!
